text.p: These are the stories making headlines in the Namibian newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
* The High Court has ordered the police to stop harassing Ovahimba people opposed to government's planned Epupa hydro- electric scheme.

* Youth and Sport deputy minister Hadino Hishongwa has defended his decision to charter Air Namibia's Jumbo Jet to take Namibian delegates to and from the World Festival for Youth and Students in Cuba, saying this was the result of a U.S. air blockade of Cuba. The trip cost taxpayers around N$3 million, money, which Hishongwa admitted, had not been budgeted for.

* Two issues regarding the situation of the Herero in Namibia surfaced yesterday, with the High Court granting the Himba an interim interdict against police harassment, while the opposition DTA of Namibia criticised the government for apparently having forbidden the Ovazemba tribe to inaugurate their own chief.

* Swapo is busy creating tribal conflict, which could have catastrophic consequences, the DTA of Namibia charged yesterday, saying the ruling party was applying double standards with regard to its own supporters and other people in the country.

* The Himba headman Hikumenue Kapika, who attracted international attention over the past months with his fight for the rights of his people, yesterday posted a victory in the Windhoek High Court with an interim interdict against unconstitutional decisions in this country.
